introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in the question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 23/0595/3/Grp 1 to Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing), Task II (spreadsheet) and Task III (a short exercise on HTML, on a database or on a C or Pascal program). The working files named in the tasks (the picture UN.jpg, the pictures of the authors) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP ONE - TASK II (20 marks)**

The worksheet below is used to record and analyze students' test and exam scores in a certain subject. Test 1 and Test 2 are each scored on 15, while Exam is scored on 20.

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2023-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_G1-T2_fig_1.png)

*Figure: the worksheet. Row 1 holds the column headings (No, Name, Test 1, Test 2, Tests Total, Exam, Term Total, Rank, Remarks in columns A to I); the seven students are in rows 2 to 8; the labels "Count Failed" and "Count Passed" are in rows 10 and 11, with an empty cell in column G beside each. Columns E, G, H and I are empty.*

incertitudes: Structure du lot : les quatre PDF fournis sont nommes DAY1 a DAY4, mais les pages de garde imprimees parlent de GROUPES (« Group Two », « Group Three », « Group Four », livrets 23/0595/3/Grp 2, 3 et 4), pas de jours. Un seul dossier, douze fichiers : numero_exercice G1-T1 a G4-T3 (groupe n, tache m), groupes ["GROUP 1"] a ["GROUP 4"] (et non D<n>-T<m> / ["DAY n"]). regles_choix est vide : le candidat ne passe qu'un seul groupe, ce qui n'est pas exprimable.

Le PDF DAY1 (Group One) n'a que 3 pages et pas de page de garde (il commence a la page 2 du livret, « Do all the tasks... ») : le niveau et la matiere sont verifies par la reference imprimee en pied de page (0000/0595/3/Grp 1, soit le code 0595) et par la structure identique aux trois autres groupes. La duree de 2 h 30 est reprise des pages de garde des groupes 2, 3 et 4 (« Two and a Half hours »).

Aucun corrige officiel n'existe : les reponses sont redigees. Les « marking ideas » sont des repartitions indicatives faites d'apres les points imprimes ; le bareme du jury n'est pas connu. Les fichiers de donnees du jour (image UN.jpg, photos des auteurs, dossier du candidat) ne sont pas dans le PDF ; aucun logiciel (traitement de texte, tableur, gestionnaire de base de donnees, navigateur, compilateur) n'a ete execute : les menus sont donnes sous leur forme generale (Office / LibreOffice recents), de memoire, sans version de logiciel affirmee.

Les filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo), les cadres d'en-tete (numero de centre, nom du candidat, « For examiners' use only »), les lignes a completer et les artefacts du scanner (scans sans couche texte, photos de feuilles legerement inclinees) sont ignores. Chaque PDF a ete lu page par page en image.

Tous les resultats chiffres (colonnes calculees, classements, comptages, totaux) ont ete recalcules avec Python a partir des donnees imprimees, en fractions exactes pour les moyennes ; les formules de tableur ont ete traduites en Python (SUM, AVERAGE, RANK, IF, COUNTIF). Les points imprimes de chaque tache somment bien au total annonce (voir ci-dessous) ; aucun point imprime n'a ete corrige.
Group One, Task II : points imprimes 4, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 4, 4 = 20, comme annonce. Le sujet imprime pour b) 2 points (formule) puis 1 point (copie) : transcrits en b1 et b2.

Figure du tableur (page 2 du PDF DAY1) : photo de la feuille, un peu inclinee et sombre ; extraite sans filigrane (calques retires, eclairage aplati, controle OCR OK). La colonne Exam apparait decalee d'une demi-ligne par l'inclinaison : elle est lue ligne a ligne, 15, 9, 12, 9, 9, 10, 7 pour Thelma, Peter, Henry, Joan, Paul, Audrey, Mispa (sept valeurs pour sept eleves). Le prenom de la derniere ligne est lu « Mispa » (ecriture floue). Les etiquettes « Count Failed / Count Passed » sont a gauche de G10 et G11, comme l'indique la question h.

Question h : le sujet demande de compter « based on the values in cells G2:G8 » (colonne Term Total), donc les seuils < 10 et >= 10 ; une autre lecture (compter les mots dans la colonne I) donne les memes resultats (3 et 4). Question g : « I3 to I8 » imprime, la formule est ecrite en I2 puis copiee jusqu'a I8. Question e : RANK en ordre decroissant (le plus haut total = rang 1), lecture usuelle.
Peter a un total de 9,83 (59/6) : tout juste sous 10, donc FAILED. Les valeurs sont donnees arrondies a 2 decimales ; elles ont ete calculees en fractions exactes (pas d'egalite de rang).

questions.corrige_markdown:
Open a spreadsheet program (for example *Microsoft Excel* or *LibreOffice Calc*) and a new workbook.

1. Key in the nine headings in row 1 (A1 to I1).
2. Key in the seven students in rows 2 to 8: the number in column A, the name in B, the two test scores in C and D and the exam score in F. Leave columns E, G, H and I empty: they are filled with formulas later.
3. Key in the two labels **Count Failed** and **Count Passed** in rows 10 and 11 (the result cells are G10 and G11).
4. Check every number against the printed worksheet (one wrong digit changes the results). Apply borders to the table, as in the figure.

Marking idea (4 marks): headings correct (1); names and numbers correct (1); scores in C, D and F correct (1); labels for the counts present (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: In cell E2, calculate the sum of Test 1 and Test 2 on 20. Use the formula $\frac{2}{3}(Test\ 1 + Test\ 2)$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each test is scored on 15, so the sum of the two tests is on 30. To bring it to a mark on 20 it is multiplied by $\frac{20}{30} = \frac{2}{3}$.

**E2: `=2/3*(C2+D2)`**

The brackets are compulsory: without them the spreadsheet would compute `2/3*C2` first and then add `D2`. For Thelma: $\frac{2}{3}(10 + 9) = \frac{38}{3} = 12.67$.

Marking idea (2 marks): sum of C2 and D2 in brackets (1); multiplication by 2/3 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Copy the formula to Cells E3:E8. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select E2, then drag the fill handle (the small square at the bottom right corner of the cell) down to E8 (or copy E2 and paste in E3:E8). The row numbers change by themselves because the references C2 and D2 are relative.

questions.enonce_markdown: Write in the space below, the formula you find in Cell E8, after copying as requested in (b) above. *[1 mark]*

After copying, the references have moved down by six rows (from row 2 to row 8):

Check: $\frac{2}{3}(11 + 11) = \frac{44}{3} = 14.67$.

Marking idea (1 mark): `=2/3*(C8+D8)`.

questions.enonce_markdown: In column G, calculate the total scores on 20 for all the students (each score in Column G is the average of the corresponding scores in Columns E and F). *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The term total is the mean of the tests mark (column E) and the exam mark (column F), both on 20. In **G2** type

**`=AVERAGE(E2,F2)`** (or `=(E2+F2)/2`)

and copy it down to G8.

Results for G2 to G8:

| Row | Student | Tests Total (E) | Exam (F) | Term Total (G) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Thelma | 12.67 | 15 | 13.83 |
| 3 | Peter | 10.67 | 9 | 9.83 |
| 4 | Henry | 14.00 | 12 | 13.00 |
| 5 | Joan | 18.00 | 9 | 13.50 |
| 6 | Paul | 7.33 | 9 | 8.17 |
| 7 | Audrey | 8.00 | 10 | 9.00 |
| 8 | Mispa | 14.67 | 7 | 10.83 |

Check for Thelma: $\frac{12.67 + 15}{2} = 13.83$. Values are shown rounded to 2 decimal places; the spreadsheet keeps the exact values (for example 9.8333... for Peter).

Marking idea (2 marks): correct formula (1); copied to all students with correct values (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: In Column H, compute the rank of each student based on the scores in Column G. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the function **RANK**, which gives the position of a value in a list (1 for the highest value). In **H2** type

**`=RANK(G2,$G$2:$G$8)`**

and copy it down to H8. The list `$G$2:$G$8` must be **fixed** (absolute reference) so that it is the same for every student; only G2 changes to G3, G4... .

Results:

| Row | Student | Term Total | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Thelma | 13.83 | 1 |
| 3 | Peter | 9.83 | 5 |
| 4 | Henry | 13.00 | 3 |
| 5 | Joan | 13.50 | 2 |
| 6 | Paul | 8.17 | 7 |
| 7 | Audrey | 9.00 | 6 |
| 8 | Mispa | 10.83 | 4 |

Marking idea (1 mark): RANK function with the fixed range G2:G8 and correct ranks.

questions.enonce_markdown: Write the name of the student who is ranked first in the space below. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The highest term total is 13.83, so the student ranked 1 is **Thelma**.

Marking idea (1 mark): Thelma.

questions.enonce_markdown: In cell I2 use the IF function to display the word "PASSED" if the Term Total is greater than or equal to 10, and the word "FAILED" otherwise. Copy the function to Cells I3 to I8. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The IF function has three parts: the test, the result if the test is true, the result if it is false. The test is on the term total in G2. In **I2** type

**`=IF(G2>=10,"PASSED","FAILED")`**

The words are in double quotation marks because they are text. "Greater than or equal to 10" is written `>=10` (not `>10`). Copy the formula down to I8.

Results:

| Row | Student | Term Total | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Thelma | 13.83 | PASSED |
| 3 | Peter | 9.83 | FAILED |
| 4 | Henry | 13.00 | PASSED |
| 5 | Joan | 13.50 | PASSED |
| 6 | Paul | 8.17 | FAILED |
| 7 | Audrey | 9.00 | FAILED |
| 8 | Mispa | 10.83 | PASSED |

Peter (9.83) is just below 10, so he FAILED. An equivalent formula is `=IF(G2<10,"FAILED","PASSED")`.

Marking idea (4 marks): IF function (1); correct condition G2>=10 (1); the two words in quotation marks in the right order (1); copied to I8 with correct results (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: In Cells G10 and G11, use the COUNTIF function to compute the number of failed and passed cases based on the values in cells G2:G8. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
COUNTIF counts the cells of a range that satisfy a condition. The condition for a pass is a term total of 10 or more; a fail is a term total below 10.

- **G10** (Count Failed): **`=COUNTIF(G2:G8,"<10")`** gives **3** (Peter, Paul and Audrey).
- **G11** (Count Passed): **`=COUNTIF(G2:G8,">=10")`** gives **4** (Thelma, Henry, Joan and Mispa).

Check: $3 + 4 = 7$, the number of students. The result agrees with the column I (three FAILED, four PASSED).

Marking idea (4 marks): COUNTIF with range G2:G8 (1); correct condition for failed (1) and for passed (1); correct results 3 and 4 (1).
